main_text.l: Exercitatio I. Dehortatio adolescentum ab affectatione Sermonis obsoleti.

Exordium sit à thesi: Nihil facilius κακοζηλία[?] : sed & nihil vanius. Ratio: Quia vitia rerum, ob naturæ corruptionem, pluribus placent, & facilius adhærent, quàm res ipsæ. Verùm à prudentioribus semper improbantur, & per se evanescunt.
Hypothesis: Ita κακοζηλία[?] Sermonis obsoleti hodie multis præsertim adolescentibus arridet admodum: Opinantibus apicem & omne, quod

page.notes: The initial E of "Exordium" is a woodcut initial, joined to the word. The Greek word κακοζηλία is partly unclear at both places; the letters were read from a small scan. The running head is faint and may read differently. Show-through from the facing page (text on the left and right margins and at the top) was left out. The page number "I" is printed at the top centre. The title block is set in capitals and spaced type. The catchword "dicitur," stands right of the signature and is not repeated in the text.
